listing_view.reasoning: Subscription reached only ~1.38x by the afternoon of the final day, which is tepid for a mainboard IPO and was below 1x until the closing day itself — that argues against any listing pop. With no grey market premium, anchor data, or retail attention figures available, there is nothing in what I was given to support a strong debut.

longterm_view.reasoning: Revenue growth is real but EBITDA margin swung from 7.01% to 4.47% to 5.42%, suggesting low and unstable pricing power typical of government/PSU project work [business, page 214]. The balance sheet deteriorated sharply — total debt roughly 3.6x'd year-on-year and debt-to-equity jumped to 0.96 — while the computed current ratio of ~0.14 implies either severe working-capital strain or a classification quirk I cannot resolve, and with no cash flow statement or ROE/ROCE printed, I cannot confirm the earnings convert to cash.

governance.reasoning: Related-party guarantees given rose from Rs 4,024.28 lakhs to Rs 7,453.38 lakhs over three years [promoters, page 329], a growing contingent exposure, though the litigation extracts assert no material SEBI or regulatory action against the company or promoters [litigation, page 387]. The extracts I hold are too thin — no promoter background or pledge detail — to score this confidently either way.

key_risks.why_it_matters: A book that only crossed 1x on the final morning signals thin institutional/retail appetite, raising the odds of a flat or negative listing.

The apparent cheapness (P/E ~19.6 vs benchmark 70.63) rests on a peer set of which zero rows could be verified, so the discount may be an artefact of cherry-picked or expensive peers.

A benchmark that high for a 5%-margin EPC-type business is itself suspicious, so the 'cheap' reading may reflect expensive or mismatched peers rather than genuine value; I was given nothing to resolve this either way.

answers.question: how is the shortfall funded?
answers.answer: If this means a subscription shortfall: the latest recorded figure is ~1.38x, so as of the last reading the issue is covered, albeit barely and only after crossing 1x on the final morning. If it means a funding shortfall in operations/working capital, the extracts do not state one; the only adjacent disclosure is that the company must maintain margins to obtain performance bank guarantees and may fail to do so. The fresh issue vs OFS split and objects of the issue were not readable from what I was given, so I cannot say who underwrites any shortfall or how proceeds are deployed.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A verified peer table showing the 70.63 benchmark is genuinely comparable, plus a cash flow statement proving EBITDA converts to operating cash despite the government receivables cycle and a stable current ratio, would lift the long-term view; strong anchor book or final-day institutional subscription data would lift the listing view.
